Less arrives needing a verdict: Accounts on the app stop sending anything that has to be interpreted. Whatever reads documents for you has a smaller and stranger pile left, which is where it earns its keep.
Quotes, payments and the store stay put: None of that is on offer here and none of it is affected. VOS hands over a finished order and takes no view on what the rest of your stack does with it.
Point it at the accounts that phone most: Adding VOS removes nothing, so begin with a handful of the kitchens that ring the desk and leave every other arrangement exactly where it is.

@graph.name: Is VOS a WizCommerce alternative, and is it better than WizCommerce?

acceptedAnswer.text: Narrower, and the difference is worth stating plainly. They take whatever arrives from an account and work the order out of it, while VOS changes what the account sends so there is nothing to work out. At getting an accurate order out of a kitchen that will not use an order form, we think VOS is better. At reading a handwritten sheet, quoting an inquiry, running a storefront, a CRM or payments, no: we do none of it and are not building any of it.

@graph.name: Do they not handle voice already?

acceptedAnswer.text: They do, and anybody claiming otherwise has not read their site: voice notes are on their own list of things the assistant reads, alongside scans and handwriting. The difference is not voice. It is that a note gets interpreted after the fact, while in VOS the speaking builds the lines and the buyer approves them before anything is sent.

@graph.name: Are they not built for food distribution too?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are, and we are not going to pretend differently. Food and beverage is one of their named industries, with promotions, warehouse-level availability and unit-of-measure pricing in it. Our claim is narrower: one step, done one way, for the accounts that ring rather than log in.

@graph.name: Who checks the order before it reaches us?

acceptedAnswer.text: In VOS it is the customer, on their own screen, before it sends. That matters because the only person who knows whether the order is right is the one who wants the goods. Be clear on the limit, though: this applies to orders placed in the app. A call or a voicemail to your desk gets no number, no timestamp and nothing moving against stock.

@graph.name: Does one of them have to go?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and we would not advise it if you have a real paperwork problem. They are aimed at different halves of it: one shrinks what arrives as a document, the other deals with what still does. Neither needs the other switched off.

They quote the platform, the same as we do. The one price they publish is for their AI photo product, which is sold on its own page with its own tiers. The one thing worth noting is scope: ours covers one step, theirs covers a product family, so you are not comparing like for like anyway.

@graph.name: How fast could this be running?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most distributors have it live in 24 to 48 hours, and most kitchens manage a first order that day. There is no model to train and nothing to connect, which is why a WizCommerce alternative gets looked at by teams who want one thing fixed this week.
